strings.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
strings.role: U.S. representative for New York's 14th congressional district
strings.summary: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is a Democratic politician who has represented New York's 14th district since 2019. She entered Congress after working in community organising and drew attention with a Green New Deal proposal linking climate action, jobs and social equity. Her work also includes committee oversight and constituent services.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through 18 November 2026, with recent congressional activity supported by the 12 November roll call. The 2026 reelection entry relies on a media race call, not official certification. Policy proposals are distinguished from enacted laws.
strings.influence.rationale: Gained international attention through Green New Deal and social equity advocacy and is a prominent figure in a new generation of American progressive politics.
strings.facts.f1.label: Higher education
strings.facts.f1.value: Graduated from Boston University in 2011 with a BA in International Relations and Economics.
strings.facts.f2.label: Early work
strings.facts.f2.value: Worked in community organising and, after college, as a bartender and waitress in New York.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Proposing a Green New Deal resolution
strings.highlights.h1.text: Introduced H.Res.109 in 2019, bringing emissions reductions, jobs and social equity into one policy framework. It was a proposed resolution, not an implemented national programme.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From grassroots campaigning to Congress
strings.highlights.h2.text: Defeated longtime incumbent Joe Crowley in the 2018 Democratic primary and then won the general election. Entering Congress at 29, she set the record at that time as its youngest woman member.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Media called another election victory
strings.timeline.t1.text: Anadolu Agency reported the following day, citing an AP race call, that she retained New York's 14th district. The report is not an election certification document.
strings.timeline.t2.title: House released Met Gala ethics report
strings.timeline.t2.text: The committee found that related gifts and payments did not comply with the rules, but found no evidence of intentional underpayment. It required an additional payment of $2,733.28 and a $250 donation as conditions for declining sanctions. The report was not a criminal conviction.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Began fourth House term
strings.timeline.t3.text: Took the oath for the 119th Congress. This term is distinct from the following term contested in the 2026 election.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Introduced Green New Deal resolution
strings.timeline.t4.text: Introduced H.Res.109, proposing a ten-year federal mobilisation for emissions reductions, jobs and equity. The resolution was referred to the relevant committees.
strings.timeline.t5.title: First entered the U.S. House
strings.timeline.t5.text: Began representing New York's 14th district at age 29. Her service began after the 2018 general election.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First elected to the U.S. House
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won a seat in the 116th Congress in the general election. The earlier Democratic primary victory had not itself put her in office.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Defeated incumbent in primary
strings.timeline.t7.text: Defeated Joe Crowley in the Democratic primary for New York's 14th district, securing the party's general-election nomination.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduated from Boston University
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed undergraduate studies in International Relations and Economics. The university biography also records an internship in Senator Edward Kennedy's immigration office.
